lines: Larsson korgmakare is in Gamla stan, Stockholm. Since 1903 we have made and restored furniture and other objects in rattan, seagrass and cord by hand.

The company KW Larsson Korgmöbelfabrik was started in 1903 by the brothers Emil and Knut Wilhelm Larsson at Jakobsbergsgatan 43 in Stockholm. They made mainly wicker chairs, for Grand Hotell Saltsjöbaden among others.

Knut Wilhelm's son John Larsson was apprenticed to a master basket maker before he began working with his father and uncle. John was interested in construction and developed the company's production of furniture in rattan. Nordiska kompaniet (NK) became a large customer for John's modern and functional furniture. Between the wars the design of furniture began to change, fewer and fewer woven wicker chairs were made and rattan became a strong competitor to willow in craft furniture making.

As early as the 1930s John Larsson met the architect Josef Frank, then newly appointed designer for Svensk Tenn. Josef Frank drew furniture in rattan, and John Larsson made it. Since then Larsson korgmakare has made Josef Frank's rattan furniture for Svenskt Tenn without interruption.
As well as being a craftsman, John Larsson was also a skilled designer, and during the 1930s–40s he drew a number of models for Larsson korgmakare, many of which are still in production today.

In 1973 John Larsson was succeeded in the firm by his son Stig Larsson, who ran the basket workshop under the name "KW Larsson Eftr." Stig Larsson went on working with architects and designed, among other things, a decoratively woven dining chair in dyed material, for Ahlsén & Lindström after a painted original by Bo Ahlsén.
In 2005 Stig's daughter Erica Larsson took over the business as a fourth-generation basket maker. The company name was changed in 1989 to "Larsson korgmakare".

Besides making its own models, Larsson korgmakare has over all these years also carried out repairs to wicker and rattan furniture, and seat weaving in rattan, seagrass and cord on furniture by Josef Frank, Carl Malmsten, Bruno Mathsson, Börge Mogensen and Hans J Wegner among others. The workshop has a unique experience of handling and carefully restoring valuable furniture. At the same time there is a commitment to reuse, which shows in the fact that no job is too small when a much-loved piece of furniture needs freshening up and mending.

An important part of the business today is commissioned work for both private and public settings. Larsson korgmakare has a long tradition of working with designers and architects' offices. Among them Josef Frank, Uno Lindh/Svenska Rum Arkitekter, Ahlsén & Lindström and Nyréns Arkitektkontor. In more recent years there are for example rattan furniture by Matti Klenell and Carina Seth Andersson for Nationalmuseum (2018).
Member of Föreningen Skråhantverkarna, www.skrahantverkarna.com Hantverkarna Stockholm, www.hantverkarna.se Hantverksvandringar i Gamla stan, www.hantverksvandringar.se
Larsson korgmakare is represented in a number of books and collections.

Example books: "Korgmöbelmakeriet i Sverige med utblickar mot övriga Norden" by Albin Tingbo, Carlssons (1999). "Svenska stolar" by Dan Gordan, Norstedts (2002). "Historiska hantverk: 20 nutidsreportage" by Samuel Karlsson, Byggförlaget (2003). "Stockholms korgmakare" by Arne Björnstad, Nordiska Museets Förlag (2009). "Svenska stolar och deras formgivare 1899–2013" by Dan Gordan, Norstedts (2014). "Verkstäder" by Cilla Ramnek, Natur & Kultur (2018).
Our own furniture is made by hand, in environmentally friendly cultivated rattan. Some ten models are in production. More models can be seen at the workshop itself.
Larsson korgmakare has solid experience of commissions for private and public settings. Among the customers are:
for the lightship Finngrundet, which is owned by Statens maritima museer and is now a museum ship (1990s). And for the lightship Almagrundet.
Half a hot-air balloon basket as a till counter
for the restaurant Kryddhyllan, Gröna Lund, Stockholm (2013).
Rattan frame for the sculpture "Vildhundens hjärta"
New production of a number of models by Josef Frank
for the exhibition "Capri" by designer Lars Nilsson for Svenskt Tenn (2018).

In the workshop all kinds of repairs to furniture in wicker and rattan are carried out. When the frame is restored, the seat rewoven or the wrapped details renewed, the piece of furniture is given new life.

Craft, sustainability and reuse are close to our hearts. Many of the pieces of furniture that come into the workshop for repair have been used and loved by their people for many years. "Can we save it?" is a common question when the owner shows us their piece of furniture. Every piece of furniture is unique, and we agree with you on the extent and form of the work and give you a price before we begin.

When we make our own furniture and Josef Frank's models for Svenskt Tenn we work in rattan pole. The hard rattan is heated over an open flame, so-called steam bending, is bent to the desired shape and dabbed with cold water until it has cooled and the shape has set. For seat weaving and wrapping with rattan we use strips cut from the skin of the rattan.

Rattan grows naturally or is cultivated together with the rubber plant in tropical countries. It is fast-growing, and is harvested at a length of about 100 metres. As far as possible we try to buy cultivated rattan. By working in cultivated rattan we can help to protect tropical forest. The price of the raw material varies, which affects our production cost. Today only a handful of makers of rattan furniture remain in Europe, one of them in Sweden; Larsson korgmakare!
Seagrass – an aquatic plant which after harvesting is dried and spun into a thread that is treated with resin. Seagrass seats are found on chair models by Börge Mogensen among others.
Paper cord – made in an environmentally friendly way from biodegradable cellulose fibre. Used for reweaving seats on for example Hans J Wegner's classic Wishbone Chair ("Y-stolen").
You are welcome to email or call us if you have questions about repairs.

For press images please contact Larsson korgmakare and we will send you login details for our image archive. When publishing images in digital media we ask you to state "Photo copyright Larsson korgmakare" where no other copyright is given.

badhusstolen-230.description: Badhusstolen 230 was ordered for Centralbadet, designed in 1904 by Wilhelm Flemming and situated at Drottninggatan 88 in Stockholm. John Larsson's armchairs were much appreciated and have been in production at Larsson korgmakare ever since.
badhusstolen-230.material: rattan produced in an environmentally friendly way
badhusstolen-230.dimensionsRaw: Height: 840 mm | Depth: 780 mm | Width: 630 mm | Seat height: 350 mm
badhusstolen-230.care: Clean with a soft cloth damped with soapy water. Wipe dry afterwards. Protect the furniture from prolonged damp, in the garden, on a terrace or a balcony.

frisorstolen-266.description: Frisörstolen 266 was drawn by John Larsson for Frisördepån. When John's son Stig met his future mother-in-law, her ladies' hairdressing salon turned out to be furnished with John's chair! The very comfortable chair is well suited to sitting in for a long time, reading for example.
